verdict.probe_answer: Both arms' tests can't literally run against the old 2-arg signature (compile error), so the real question is whether they'd catch bugs in a wrong 4-arg reimplementation. Both include the spec-mandated `commit_precedence_and_comment_only_falls_back_to_title` verbatim (strongest test in each) — it locks in Typed>File>Title>Derived and comment-only-is-absent, and would fail against any wrong ordering or a naive strip-without-recheck implementation. Arm A's weakest test is the carried-over `commit_message_file_else_fallback`: fine for file-vs-title/blank handling, but nothing exercises comment+text mixed, NUL bytes, or the 64KiB bound, despite Arm A implementing byte-safe bounding in code — that correctness win goes unverified. Arm B adds three more edge tests (partial-comment-in-text, NUL stripping, 64KiB bound), giving broader path coverage; its strongest addition, `commit_candidate_strips_partial_comment_not_absent`, would genuinely fail if strip-vs-reject logic were wrong. Its weakest is `commit_candidate_bounded_to_64kib_not_rejected`: it repeats ASCII 'x', where char-count and byte-count coincide, so it passes even though Arm B's impl (`.chars().take(65536)`) bounds by *characters*, not bytes — a candidate of 70000 multi-byte chars (e.g. 'é') would come out over 64KiB, the exact bug this test claims to guard against. Arm A has no bounding test but its implementation is actually correct.
verdict.rationale: Both arms nail the signature, precedence, comment-stripping, main.rs/merge.rs call sites, and the spec's required test verbatim. Two concrete differences: (1) 64KiB bounding — Arm A truncates by bytes with UTF-8 boundary walk-back (correct); Arm B truncates via `.chars().take(65536)`, bounding by character count, which can exceed 64KiB in bytes for multi-byte UTF-8 — a real violation of the explicit spec requirement, masked by Arm B's own ASCII-only test. (2) decide() fidelity — Arm A propagates `CommitSource` into decide's signature everywhere, which forced editing tweak.rs, a file the task explicitly said was 'not a caller... leave it' (minor scope slip, though the resulting change is itself correct). Arm B avoids touching tweak.rs but hardcodes `false` for decide's second tuple field at the main.rs call site instead of deriving it from the already-computed `commit_source`, silently discarding real information (should be `commit_source == CommitSource::Derived`) — a plausible latent bug if decide ever reads that field. Net: Arm A has one small, harmless scope deviation; Arm B has two real code-correctness defects, despite writing more edge-case tests overall.
